subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should OpenClaw make `chat.send` ACK imply durable user-turn visibility/progress, or is the current UI-side pending/history preservation sufficient for this issue?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses the gateway runtime contract, transcript ownership, latency, and duplicate-suppression boundaries; automation should not pick that product/API contract while the direct PR is still unresolved.

options.title: Require gateway durability/progress
options.body: Keep this issue open until a focused gateway change or narrowed replacement for the candidate PR proves that accepted WebChat user turns are durable or visibly failed after ACK.

options.title: Accept UI-only mitigation
options.body: Treat the current pending-send and optimistic-history preservation as sufficient, then close or retarget the gateway-side PR as not required for this issue.

options.title: Narrow the candidate PR first
options.body: Ask the candidate PR author or an owner to split the durable user-turn persistence slice from broader Pi/session changes before deciding final acceptance.

recommendation.title: Require gateway durability/progress
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a focused gateway change or narrowed replacement for the candidate PR proves that accepted WebChat user turns are durable or visibly failed after ACK.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the gateway `chat.send` contract and transcript/session ownership, where history shows repeated foundational work by this owner.
